relevance_note: The paper describes identifiable GFAP variant carriers, e.g. 'The proband from Family 3 was heterozygous for a synonymous variant NM_001363846.1:c.1290C>A; p.(Arg430Arg)'.
method_note: Read the paper by hand; a short script assembled the JSON from hand-chosen spans and labels (no table transcription; the paper has no tables). Supplementary Table S1 (per-person clinical data for Families 1 and 3 and the prior c.1289G>A cases) and Supp. Figure S1 are not in the file ('**Supp info**' only), so most per-person detail is unavailable. Family 1 (>20 affected; group counts such as 'gait dysfunction (12/16)', 'MRI ... in 6 individuals', 'Autopsy performed in two affected individuals', 'all six tested members ... heterozygous') is described only at group level; those people get no rows except the individually identifiable 'one affected individual from Family 1' who was sequenced (unnamed person 2) and the deceased member whose autopsy RNA was studied (F1-1, label from Figure 2). These two may be the same person; the paper does not say, so they are kept separate. F1-1's variant row comes from the abstract statement about 'Affected members of Family 1'; zygosity is left not reported because F1-1 is not stated to be among the tested members. F2-1 (proband of Family 2, label from Figure 2D) was 'previously reported as Patient 43 in Li et al. (2005)'; this is first-hand description, so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' and the citation is in publications.prior_report_citation. The three affected siblings of F2-1 have no stated sex and are not stated to have been tested (only the proband of Family 2 was sequenced), so they get no variant rows despite the abstract's 'Affected members of Family 1 and Family 2 shared the same missense variant'. Family 3 proband is 'unnamed person 1' (the paper uses only 'the proband'). The Family 3 Simoa result ('one individual in Family 3') does not say which person, so it is not assigned. Previously published c.1289G>A carriers (Melchionda sibling pair; Karp; Pinto e Vairo) are included because the paper gives the variant for them; the paper notes the Pinto e Vairo individual may be related to Family 1. Their transcript/protein are left not reported because the passage prints only 'c.1289G>A'. c.1290C>A is called 'synonymous' by the authors; recorded as variant type 'other'. The father's variant type, transcript and protein are left not reported because his sentence prints only 'c.1290C>A'. 'upper motor neurological signs' was mapped to the checklist item 'spasticity or pyramidal signs'; 'gastric dysmotility' was not counted as bowel dysfunction; frontal-horn T_2 signal was not mapped to periventricular rim or white matter. Three unrelated AxD control brains in the western blot and the ClinVar/Li et al. variants c.1171+5G>A and c.731C>T (no person described) get no rows. No contradictions found.
